title: Platform Troubleshooting 1
description: Users can launch Windows on AVD, but several internal web applications will not load. Service Desk has a high volume of calls.
scope: Out-of-hours Sev1: AVD sessions succeed; internal web applications fail from inside those sessions.
illustrativeDisclaimer: This scenario, its mock incident, runbook titles, product names, escalation routes, and organisational procedures are illustrative. Validate them against approved operational sources before use. They are not bank-specific policy.
assessorGuidance: The desktop broker is probably not the fault. Reward splitting AVD health from name resolution and egress path (DNS, Prisma/Secure Access, firewall). Do not penalise engaging network or security teams. Safety-critical: do not disable security inspection or open Any/Any rules to 'test'.
acceptableAlternativeApproaches: Name-resolution first (nslookup from a session host), then egress/proxy path, then firewall change calendar.
Comparing a working physical-PC path vs AVD path to isolate VDI egress.
Checking a second application on the same VIP versus a distinct application to see if the fault is shared infrastructure.

initialIncident.callSummary: 01:07 UTC, Saturday. Users can launch Windows on HP01 and HP02, but internal web apps will not load in Edge. Service Desk has 40+ calls.

serviceNow.caller: Service Desk on behalf of Payments Operations
serviceNow.shortDescription: Multiple business web apps unreachable from AVD sessions
serviceNow.description: Desktop connect OK. Internal HTTPS apps fail. Microsoft 365 from the same desktop is OK. First user report 00:51 UTC.

impact.customers: AVD users needing internal web apps; payments operations overnight team blocked.
impact.colleagues: Service Desk. Application support on standby.
impact.business: Overnight payments exception handling cannot proceed. Illustrative impact only.

facts.label: Failing
facts.value: Internal web apps will not load in Edge. Service Desk has 40+ calls. Payments Portal, HR Self-Service, overnight batch console among those named.

facts.label: Still working
facts.value: Users can launch Windows on HP01 and HP02. Some say Outlook on the web still works from the same session.

facts.label: When
facts.value: Saturday 01:07 UTC. First user report 00:51 UTC.

questions.prompt: Walk through how you would handle this incident from the first call through to recovery. Write the full response in your own words.
questions.helpText: The desktop launches. The apps do not. Think about what you would split, and who you would involve, before you change the platform.
questions.assessorGuidance: Score the whole write-up. Reward splitting working desktops from a failed application path; DNS then timeout/path/Secure Access rather than rebuilding hosts or resetting profiles; handing the change and connector to network/security with MIM on a Sev1; not disabling inspection or opening Any/Any to test; Microsoft AVD support only if evidence later points at Azure; a factual update; and recovery confirmed with a probe from a session host plus a real user opening the app. Do not score as demonstrated: redeploying the pool, detaching inspection yourself, or closing on a closed change ticket without a user test.

scoringCriteria.label: Separates desktop availability from application-path impact
Manages Sev1 with MIM and an evidence-based handover
Judges Microsoft engagement against evidence rather than habit
Does not treat a working host pool as the object to rebuild
Investigates DNS, then path/firewall/Secure Access, with appropriate evidence
Uses application-access runbook and change information
Engages network/security rather than making unauthorised path changes
Clear operational updates and user-confirmed recovery
